model.description: MODEL_CLOSER — REQUIRED, no default: a model default in code is how a run silently measures a different model than the report claims (P5 finding). Here it would also revoke a ruling: Q9 decides the close pass runs on a strong model, and a close pass that quietly falls back to a cheap one measures nothing and sharpens less than it costs

provider_extra.description: The provider overlay of this cell. Its one knob is the deliberation budget at provider_extra.reasoning.effort (MEMORY_REASONING_CLOSE) — set explicitly, never inherited from the provider default, and NOT minimal: a strong model asked to sharpen a session it is seeing whole is not a minimal-effort call. Declared as the overlay rather than as the flat `reasoning_effort` param because the overlay is applied last and wins over that param anyway; a setting named after the flat param would name a field this cell does not set.

description.purpose: Reads a CLOSED session whole and sharpens what the turns left rough. Per-turn annotation (#298) is fast and blind in one direction: the front model annotates the turn it has just answered and cannot know the turn after it, so a correction three turns later, a value the conversation only settled at the end and a claim the session itself retracted all land as they were first said. This cell is the one place that sees the session as a whole, and Q9 rules its model class: one strong-model call per close.
description.use_when: Called by close-glue exactly once per closed session, with the session's turns and the open facts they produced in the prompt. Never per turn — the whole value of this call is that the turns are already over.
description.not_in_scope: It does not EXTRACT. A turn nobody annotated stays unannotated: reading the session again to mine it for facts the front model missed would rebuild the batch lane wave 5 deleted, on a more expensive tier. Its four-point contract is what makes that distinction checkable rather than a matter of tone. No store access either, and no writing of its own: what it proposes goes to the inline ingress, which canonicalises, deduplicates and supersedes it like any other block.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one assistant turn holding the sharpening JSON. hop.finish_reason='error' is not a crash — close-glue closes the pass, says so on the report lane and leaves every fact the turns already wrote exactly as it found it.
description.consumes_meaning: system.instructions.text: the four-point contract of the pass (what may be sharpened, what may be closed, what must be left alone, and the JSON shape). messages[]: one user turn with the session's turns and its open facts as JSON.
examples: a session whose second turn said "I live in Berlin" and whose ninth said "actually I moved to Lisbon last month" -> the pass closes the first statement against the second instead of leaving two open claims on one axis
a session that mentioned a date only in passing ("since the spring") and pinned it later ("March 3rd") -> the same fact with a valid_from the turn-local annotation could not have known
a session where nothing was left rough -> an empty proposal. The pass ran, cost one call and changed nothing, and that is a correct outcome, not a failure
